we found superconducting sulfur hydrides at high pressure and high temperature.
we found superconducting hydrides with Tc up to 190 K in a wide range from H2S to H2S+H2, and the superconductivity is likely associated with the formation of SHn hydrides.

(1) sulfur hydride is a metal at P>90 GPa; (2) superconductivity occurs at Tc~150 K in H2S metal; (3) superconductivity in H2S is likely associated with dissociation of H-S bond and formation of SHx hydrides.

the search for new high-temperature superconductors.
the superconducting properties of sulfur hydride under pressure.
the discovery and study of the highest Tc superconductivity in sulfur hydride.

we have observed the highest Tc superconductivity in the conventional sense, i.e. in a metal with strong coupling between electrons, and phonons, which is in agreement with the BCS theory.
the highest Tc is achieved in H2S, but it should be noted that this is the first experiment on H2S at these high pressures.
conventional superconductivity has been observed at Tc=190 K in H2S at high pressure and high temperature, which is a record for all known superconductors.

the high Tc superconductivity has been found in a new material, and it has the highest Tc in the world.
superconductivity with the highest Tc has been observed in H2S at high pressures.
we discovered the highest critical temperature of conventional superconductivity.

the superconductivity with high Tc in hydrogen dominant materials is possible.
